title: Approve safe-to-share wording for top Known Issues pages + define publish vs internal policy
creator: Chris Osei
body:
## Context
As part of the Escalation Playbook v2 + Known-Issues sprint, Support and Docs are publishing a curated set of high-volume issues with validated mitigations. We need an explicit policy for what content is:
- safe-to-share publicly (Help Center / docs.redwoodinference.com)
- safe-to-share in 1:1 customer comms only (e.g., enterprise thread)
- internal-only (Confluence)
- restricted (need-to-know; e.g., security-sensitive, exploitability risk, customer-identifying details)

This ticket covers (1) approval of safe-to-share wording for the top Known Issues pages shipping in the first wave and (2) a lightweight decision rubric + review process so we don’t re-litigate case-by-case.

## In scope (wave 1 pages)
1) Streaming disconnects + reconnect guidance (Hosted/Dedicated)
2) 429 throttling + quota/rate-limit misconfiguration (Hosted)
3) Dedicated capacity latency spikes / noisy-neighbor symptoms + mitigations (Dedicated)
4) Private SSO/SAML login failures (Private) — policy decision: public vs internal-only summary

## Goals
- Reduce escalations by letting Support send consistent, approved mitigations immediately.
- Avoid publishing content that increases security risk, violates contracts, or exposes internal architecture details.
- Make the boundary between incident/status comms and known-issues docs explicit.

## Decision rubric (proposed)
### Publish publicly (Help Center / docs)
Publish if ALL are true:
- Workaround is validated and low-risk (does not reduce security posture, does not require privileged access, does not instruct customers to weaken auth, disable audit logs, or bypass controls).
- Steps do not expose internal-only endpoints, infrastructure identifiers, or capacity/region routing policies beyond what is already public.
- Issue is common and not customer-specific; repro doesn’t require sensitive logs.
- Wording can be generalized (no ticket references, no customer names, no timestamps that could deanonymize).

### Keep internal (Confluence) but allow a safe excerpt for customers
Keep internal if ANY are true:
- Diagnostics require internal dashboards, internal feature flags, backend request traces, or non-public config.
- Workaround is valid but could be misapplied and cause regressions/cost blowups (e.g., aggressive retries without caps; changing timeouts without guidance).
- We need flexibility because behavior is changing quickly (runtime rollout, model routing changes) and a public doc would churn weekly.

### Restricted (Security / need-to-know)
Restricted if ANY are true:
- Potential exploitability or security regression if published (auth bypass vectors, SSO misconfig patterns that help attackers, known vulnerable versions, detailed error signatures that aid enumeration).
- Includes customer-identifying information or private deployment topology.
- Under active incident response or vulnerability management where comms are controlled.

## Proposed review & ownership process
- Draft owner: Docs (Elliot Price / Wei Chen / Kira Thompson)
- Validation owner: Support Engineering (Priya Shah / Owen Phillips)
- Approval owners:
  - Product (this ticket) approves the publish-vs-internal decision and final safe-to-share language.
  - Security (Marcus Lin) reviews anything touching auth/SSO, audit logs, rate limit enforcement details, or private deployment admin guidance.
- Cadence: monthly sweep of published known-issues pages + ad-hoc review if a page changes meaningfully (new mitigations, new constraints).
- Required tags on every known-issue page (internal + public): applicability (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), impacted regions/models (if safe), first-seen date range (month), last-validated date, and a clear “when to escalate” section.

## Copy guidance (safe-to-share)
- Avoid:
  - promising ETAs
  - naming individual customer incidents
  - naming internal dashboards, alert names, or oncall rotations
  - giving step-by-step instructions that weaken security controls
- Prefer:
  - symptom-based troubleshooting
  - bounded mitigations (with caps/limits)
  - “If X persists for >Y minutes or impacts production traffic, contact Support with request IDs”

## Acceptance criteria
- [x] Decide publish vs internal-only for each wave-1 known issue page.
- [x] Provide final approved safe-to-share wording (or required edits) for wave-1 pages.
- [x] Define a repeatable publish/review checklist and owners; link it from Known Issues index.
- [x] Identify any restricted content that must stay out of public docs and how Support should communicate it (approved 1:1 excerpt, or ‘contact Support’ language).

## Links / artifacts
- Docs PR: github/redwood-docs/pr_642 (KB pages)
- SDK PR (retry/backoff messaging): github/redwood-sdk-python/pr_519
- Known-issues sprint umbrella: ENG-2841
- Incident comms alignment: sources/confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/status-page-and-comms/support-escalation-comms-alignment.json

## Final decisions (to be reflected in docs + Confluence)
1) Streaming disconnects: PUBLIC (safe-to-share). Include client-side reconnect pattern, idempotency note, recommended timeouts, and required log fields. Exclude internal error budget thresholds and internal metrics.
2) 429 throttling/quota: PUBLIC (safe-to-share). Include exponential backoff + jitter, max retry guidance, how to check org/project limits in Console, and when to request a quota increase. Exclude details of enforcement internals and any org-specific quota numbers.
3) Dedicated latency spikes/noisy neighbor: HYBRID. Public doc can include symptom triage + customer-safe mitigations (autoscaling knobs exposed to customer, routing/fallback configuration that is part of product), plus “contact Support for deeper investigation.” Keep internal runbook details (cluster-level attribution, noisy neighbor identification, node/tenant mapping) internal.
4) Private SSO/SAML failures: INTERNAL + RESTRICTED appendix. Publish a short public ‘SSO troubleshooting checklist’ ONLY if Security approves. For now, keep the detailed SSO failure modes and log patterns internal; provide Support with an approved customer-facing checklist focusing on correct metadata/certs/clock skew and “how to collect logs” without exposing sensitive error signatures.

Owner follow-ups: Docs to update page headers with classification tags; Support to align macro snippets to approved language; Security to provide a 1-paragraph safe excerpt template for SSO cases.
comments: 2026-02-13 (Chris Osei): Created per kickoff action item. Requesting Product+Security sign-off before Docs PR merges. Primary question: do we publish anything about Private SSO/SAML beyond ‘contact Support’?

2026-02-14 (Elliot Price): Draft language ready in redwood-docs/pr_642. Marked sections in the PR description as ‘needs policy decision’ (Dedicated latency spikes: what can we say about isolation/noisy neighbor?).

2026-02-16 (Priya Shah): Validation notes: streaming reconnect guidance is solid; added explicit cap on retries + suggestion to log request_id + response headers. For 429 doc, please avoid implying that higher quotas are immediate; recommend framing as ‘Support can review’.

2026-02-18 (Marcus Lin): Security review: OK to publish general SSO checklist, but do not publish concrete error codes/signatures for SAML assertions or details that enable account enumeration. Also avoid recommending disabling SSO enforcement or weakening MFA for debugging. Prefer ‘rotate cert / verify ACS URL / verify IdP clock skew’ style guidance.

2026-02-20 (Naomi Feldman): Proposed decisions: streaming + 429 = public; Dedicated latency spikes = hybrid; Private SSO detailed page stays internal, with a short customer checklist excerpt approved by Security. Please ensure every public page has a clear ‘When to contact Support’ section and avoids architecture specifics.

2026-02-24 (Wei Chen): Updated PR with requested edits (removed internal metric names, simplified dedicated wording, added escalation section). Also added page metadata: last validated, applicability, safe-to-share flag. Ready for final approval.

2026-02-26 (Naomi Feldman): Approved. Dedicated doc: keep ‘noisy neighbor’ term but define it generically as ‘contention during peak load’; removed reference to per-node attribution. Private SSO: publish only the generic checklist; keep failure-mode taxonomy internal. Marking PM-613 as done once Docs PR merges and Known Issues index links to policy checklist.
2026-03-03 (Chris Osei): Confirmed docs PR merged and Known Issues index updated with classification tags + review checklist. Closing.
